description:
WRONG, AND WITHDRAWN. Both claims in the original description were artifacts of
testing a STALE BINARY.

The runtime library is `include_str!`'d into the compiler, so editing a
`.fz` module and re-running `./target/debug/fz2` without `cargo build`
exercises the PREVIOUS library. Every 'obscure internal error' I attributed to
the two causes below came from that.

Re-tested with a real rebuild:

  * a call to a function that does not exist gives a proper diagnostic, with
    the file and the line:

        error[resolve/unknown-import]: module `Atom` does not export `from_binary/1`
          --> runtime:String.fz:298:22

  * an extern declared `:: atom` works and returns an atom (`:hi`).

fz-5xp.66 is a REAL instance of the contentless
`internal/post-resolution-leftover` error and was re-verified on a fresh build
with user code, where staleness cannot apply. It stands on its own.

Kept rather than deleted as the record of a false finding: the lesson is that a
runtime-library change needs a rebuild before it is tested, and that this error
message is contentless enough to absorb any explanation offered for it.

comments.text:
SECOND INSTANCE, same message, different cause -- which is the point.

    extern "fz" fn fz_binary_to_atom(any) :: atom

`atom` is not one of the extern return types (`ExternTy` has Binary, CString,
I64, F64, Any, Unit). Declaring it produced the SAME error as the unresolved
call, with the same empty location:

    error[internal/post-resolution-leftover]: quoted function decode failed:
      invalid any value ref: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(15), found: ValueKind(3) }
      --> <generated>

Two unrelated mistakes in a runtime-library module -- a call to a function that
does not exist, and an extern return type that is not supported -- are
indistinguishable at the surface, and neither names the module, the function or
the line. Both cost a bisection to find.

So this is not one missing diagnostic; it is a path with NO diagnostic, where
every way of being wrong arrives as the same internal decode failure. Whatever
fix lands should make the two say different things, and both should name where
they are.

title: RETRACTED: was a stale binary, not a missing diagnostic
